title: My peer and I built a no-code quant terminal for portfolio growth modeling. Looking for feedback/testers
author: NanoQuant
selftext:
**TL;DR:** My peer and I built [**NanoQuant Terminal**](https://www.nanoquant.dev/terminal)

to bring institutional-grade portfolio modeling to regular investors—without needing a $24k Bloomberg terminal or a Python degree. Looking for honest feedback!



Hey everyone,

My peer and I have been building a project for a while now, and we finally felt like it was ready to share with people who actually follow the markets.

Basically, we got frustrated by the massive gap in financial tools. On one end, you have standard stock tracking apps that just show basic line charts. On the other end, if you actually want to model portfolio growth using real quantitative methods, you’re stuck dropping thousands on enterprise software or spending hours writing clunky Python scripts.

So we built [**NanoQuant Terminal**](https://www.nanoquant.dev/terminal)

to bridge that gap, and it's completely free.



The goal is to take complex financial modeling and make it something an everyday investor can easily use to project and understand their portfolio growth. That said, we didn't water it down—there’s an advanced model so you can still run serious scenario testing and stress-test your holdings if you want to dig deeper.

We’re at the stage where we really need real user feedback to figure out what to build next.

If you have a minute, try it out at [**https://www.nanoquant.dev/terminal**](https://www.nanoquant.dev/terminal)

and let us know what you think. Test your own portfolio, and tell us where we can improve and let us know if there's anything else you'd like included—we just want to make this as useful as possible.



Thanks!

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: growth projections live or die on the return assumption. if the advanced model samples history, run 2000-2009 through it and show that to people, that decade changes how someone holds more than any chart.

comments.author: investigatormaker
comments.body:
The first thing a quant-minded tester will ask of NanoQuant Terminal is what sits under the projection: which return and volatility inputs, over which historical window, whether it simulates paths or extends a trend, and whether fees, dividends and inflation are in. Put those assumptions right beside the growth chart. A strong credibility check would be running the model from a past date and plotting what the portfolio actually did. For feedback you can act on, ask testers one thing: did the projected range for their own holdings look plausible, and if not, which way was it off?

comments.body: Everyone will say it but return beats all. Make users know quick figures and data as to why your tool works well. I have a private 500+ session backtest process coupled with live session replays myself. I would be curious how both fare against each other.
